To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Mqn (n=2, 3) films can be successfully deposited on transparent and semiconductor substrates by PVD technique.

1. the PVD technique is a suitable method to produce high quality organometallic film, 2. the structural properties of the Mqn films are strongly connected with morphology of the film and 3. the temperature of annealed films is a crucial parameter to obtain the stable and high quality films.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the structural and the optical properties of the organometallic Mqn films deposited on transparent and semiconductor substrates using Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) method.
the development of the new materials with high structural and optical properties, which are suitable for application in optoelectronic devices, especially organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs).
the development and characterization of new thin organic films for optoelectronic and photonic devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the annealing process is an important parameter in the preparation of thin films containing organometallic complexes.
the annealing process is a very important step in the fabrication of the films and its influence on the optical properties is very strong.

PVD technique is very useful to produce high quality films with a high degree of homogeneity, but the morphology of the films is strongly connected with the temperature during the deposition and annealing processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the annealing process is an important factor for improving the stability of the thin films and their optical properties.
the Mqn (n=2 or 3), M = Zn, Cu, Al films exhibit good structural quality, but the morphology can be improved using an appropriate annealing temperature.
PVD technique can be used to grow thin films of Mqn and these films exhibit high structural and optical quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Mqn (n=2 or 3; M=Zn, Cu or Al) thin films are very promising candidates for optoelectronic and photovoltaic devices.
the Mqn thin films are promising materials for applications in optoelectronic devices, such as OLEDs and solar cells.
the annealing process can significantly change the morphology and optical properties of thin films.
